question: How many civil society organisations in the EU receive more than 50 % of their funding from the EU budget, in particular through programmes such as the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme, the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund, Horizon Europe or Erasmus+?
How many of these organisations received more than EUR 500 000 per year in EU funding between 2018 and 2024?
Which projects of these organisations have been funded in the areas of migration and integration, and with which primary objectives?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.8.2025) The Commission´s accounting system groups the legal entities funded by the Commission according to certain categories1. ‘Civil society organisations’ are not a category on their own but part of one or another category, with no specific split per entity within that category.

For this reason, the Commission is not in a position to provide an exhaustive overview of the support from the EU budget provided to ‘civil society organisations. The Commission´s Financial Transparency system2 publicly shows the EU funding received by a given beneficiary and beneficiary type, also below EUR 500 000.
Where an organisation is listed in the Transparency Register3, it must publish EU funding received, which can thus be verified as well.

Moreover, the projects awarded under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme4, the Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund5, Horizon Europe6, and Erasmus+7 during the years from 2018 to 2024, including their beneficiary(ies) and the EU contribution awarded per entity are publicly available on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal in the section Projects & Results8.
